evidence.conclusion: The explicit genus transfer yields 3α(k)+1=k^{O(k)} from the planar distance-k algorithm; the ratio is independent of genus, while the rounds may depend on g and k.

comparisons.conclusion: Bounded-expansion distance-r domination uses O(r² log n) rounds and does not dominate rounds independent of n.
The k- and 3k-round points require girth at least 4k+3, a restriction absent from the full bounded-genus class.
The parameter-round distance algorithm requires K₂,t minor exclusion; the approximation scheme has log-star dependence on n.
Ordinary MDS results do not dominate a theorem for general distance k.

limits: No tightness or optimal g,k round dependence is certified.
Special parameter values, including ordinary MDS at k=1, can have better numerical ratios.
The ratio depends on k, so the constant-approximation-ratio filter must still exclude it.
